cases.prompt: A senolytic reduces marker-positive cells and improves grip strength in one mouse cohort but raises mortality in another strain. Outline a replication and mechanism study that could support or refute a tissue-specific benefit-risk claim.

rubric.criterion: Pre-specifies strain/sex/tissue strata and functional plus survival/toxicity endpoints
Uses multiple senescence-state measures and cell-target engagement
Includes randomized blinded replication, exposure/safety measures, and appropriate interaction analysis

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Surrogate-evidence dossier · milestone 1: Endpoints, nulls and interval widths. The project compares fictional observational Study A with randomized studies B and C in different model contexts; all estimates and intervals are supplied synthetic teaching values, with no human-health conclusion. For project studies A–C, label each endpoint and comparison, identify its null value and mark which supplied intervals exclude it. Keep marker units, functional assay points and survival hazard ratios separate. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Uses the correct null for each effect scale.
Distinguishes an unmeasured endpoint from an estimated interval crossing its null.
Does not rank unlike endpoint scales by raw numerical size.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Surrogate-evidence dossier · milestone 2: Association and intervention evidence. The project compares fictional observational Study A with randomized studies B and C in different model contexts; all estimates and intervals are supplied synthetic teaching values, with no human-health conclusion. Classify project Study A’s design and write the narrowest association statement. Give one confounding or selection explanation compatible with its age association, then state why that comparison does not validate an intervention surrogate. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Names the age-group comparison and observational design.
Separates statistical association from an intervention or mediation claim.
Identifies the new context and outcome evidence a surrogate claim would require.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Surrogate-evidence dossier · milestone 3: A marker response without resolved benefit. The project compares fictional observational Study A with randomized studies B and C in different model contexts; all estimates and intervals are supplied synthetic teaching values, with no human-health conclusion. Write the narrowest supported statement for project Study B, separating marker response from function and survival uncertainty. Explain why the marker result alone cannot stand in for a meaningful outcome and why the other intervals do not prove exact absence. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Reports all endpoints rather than selecting only the marker result.
Keeps unresolved intervals distinct from demonstrated equivalence.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Surrogate-evidence dossier · milestone 4: Outcome signals without a resolved marker change. The project compares fictional observational Study A with randomized studies B and C in different model contexts; all estimates and intervals are supplied synthetic teaching values, with no human-health conclusion. For project Study C, distinguish the marker, function and survival statements supported by their supplied intervals. Explain the challenge it poses to an unqualified universal marker surrogate claim, while keeping hazard, lifespan and human translation separate. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: States the functional and hazard-ratio evidence without inventing a duration effect.
Describes a null-crossing marker interval as uncertain rather than exactly zero.
Keeps the conclusion inside the fictional model comparison.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Surrogate-evidence dossier · milestone 5: Surrogate validation and a bounded dossier. The project compares fictional observational Study A with randomized studies B and C in different model contexts; all estimates and intervals are supplied synthetic teaching values, with no human-health conclusion. Assemble the project A–C evidence map. Decide what the dossier can and cannot establish about surrogate validity, name at least two missing forms of evidence, and add a two-sentence scope note preventing any fictional model-organism result from becoming a human-health or intervention recommendation. Use the project guide in week 14 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Integrates association, marker response and meaningful outcomes without collapsing their roles.
Defines the intended context and names missing measurement/outcome validation evidence.
Avoids head-to-head ranking, universal surrogacy and human-health conclusions unsupported by the dossier.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.
